note: Literature establishes premature alopecia and spondylosis as characteristic hallmarks of HTRA1-related CARASIL that are absent in NOTCH3 arteriopathies, serving as key discriminators.

evidence.text: CARASIL is characterized by low back pain and alopecia alongside cognitive decline and white matter changes, distinguishing its clinical features from NOTCH3-related arteriopathy (CADASIL).

source.title: Cadasil and Carasil
source.quote: In rare, recessively inherited CARASIL the clinical picture and white matter changes are similar as in CADASIL, but cognitive decline begins earlier. In addition, gait disturbance, low back pain and alopecia are characteristic features. CARASIL is caused by mutations (presently n = 10) in high-temperature requirement. evidence.text: Premature baldness and severe low back pain or spondylosis deformans are hallmark manifestations of CARASIL (caused by HTRA1 mutations), distinguishing it from CADASIL caused by NOTCH3.

source.title: Cerebral autosomal recessive arteriopathy with subcortical infarcts and leukoencephalopathy (CARASIL): from discovery to gene identification
source.quote: The main clinical manifestations of CARASIL are ischemic stroke or stepwise deterioration in brain functions, progressive dementia, premature baldness, and attacks of severe low back pain or spondylosis deformans/disk herniation.
